Sanitized visual observation from operator-provided nRF Connect Android screenshots, 2026-10-20.
This is a service-discovery UI observation, not a packet capture or attribute-value export.
No device addresses, full device names, identifiers, keys or raw report payloads retained.

Visible primary service: Human Interface Device, UUID 0x1812.
Visible characteristic rows within that service:
- Protocol Mode, UUID 0x2a4e: READ, WRITE.
- Report, UUID 0x2a4d: NOTIFY, READ.
  Visible descriptors: Client Characteristic Configuration 0x2902; Report Reference 0x2908.
- Report, UUID 0x2a4d: READ, WRITE.
  Visible descriptors: Client Characteristic Configuration 0x2902; Report Reference 0x2908.
- Report Map, UUID 0x2a4b: READ.
- HID Information, UUID 0x2a4a: READ.
- HID Control Point, UUID 0x2a4c: WRITE.

Two Report characteristic rows are visible; their shared UUID is not a unique endpoint identity.
Only one of these rows advertises NOTIFY. Neither Report Reference value was captured.
Do not classify the second Report as Output versus Feature without its reference value.
No Report Map, characteristic/descriptor handles, instance IDs or notification values were captured.
This does not validate raw GATT input, Switch transport or completion/notification ownership.

Security/lifecycle observations:
- Earlier screenshot: CONNECTED, BONDING...
- Later screenshot: DISCONNECTED, NOT BONDED.
A bonding procedure was observed in progress; no completed bond is shown.
The initiator and reason for bonding, and whether the operator cancelled a prompt, are unknown.
The later state is app-reported disconnected/not bonded; it is not proof of global radio cleanup.
No claim is made that the app/platform performed no automatic reads, writes or security operations.
Further requests were initially deferred while the bonding origin was unknown.

Follow-up screenshots and operator clarification, later on 2026-10-20:
- Operator explicitly reports accepting the pairing prompt.
- Earlier follow-up screenshot: CONNECTED, BONDED.
- Later follow-up screenshot: DISCONNECTED, BONDED.
- The same six characteristic rows and two Report rows remain visible.
This confirms an operator-accepted bond and an app-reported connected state, then
an app-reported disconnected state with the bond retained. It does not establish
that all attributes require bonding, or explain a Switch connection error.
No keys were requested or inspected; no bond removal/reset was requested.
No characteristic or descriptor values are visible in these follow-up images.
Before future Switch/Stadia trials, Android Bluetooth must also be off to avoid
this newly bonded host automatically reconnecting. Disconnect is not unpair.

Attempted Report Reference read, subsequently reported by operator:
- Tapping read produced no visible descriptor value.
- App log reported an exception requiring BLUETOOTH_PRIVILEGED.
- No Report ID/type bytes or other raw GATT input values were obtained.
Android 16 AOSP GattService restricts HID Report characteristic handles and their
associated descriptors. readDescriptor checks the local privileged permission
before dispatching its native read. Its permission check has no bond exemption.
The reported failure is an Android app-access restriction, not a remote ATT
error or proof that the descriptor is unreadable on other hosts.
Do not retry, change bonds, request a permission grant, or use an older-target
APK as a workaround; older-target exception suppression still skips the read.
Source: https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/Bluetooth/+/refs/heads/android16-release/android/app/src/com/android/bluetooth/gatt/GattService.java
